A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dream4Drive and DriveObj3D. The complete main text and Appendices A–F are readable and matchable, including all 18 figures and 11 tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes detection and tracking experiments, generation-quality measurements, ablations, and qualitative examples in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including downstream performance, generation quality, and insertion and guidance-map ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix A retain the same scene-editing pipeline, guidance maps, fusion adapter, diffusion architecture, training losses, and DriveObj3D asset-generation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nuScenes coverage for generation, detection, and tracking, the same asset categories, and the same insertion and corner-case scenarios, including Appendix D.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 1–5 and 10, including Panacea, SubjectDrive, Naive Insert, Trellis, and Hunyuan3D in their respective comparisons. The new related-work citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The nuScenes splits, 420-sample augmentation, training-epoch comparisons, resolutions, evaluation metrics, and testing procedures remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices A–C.

E4.justification: Both retain the insertion-position, distance, and asset-source ablations in Table 5, guidance-map ablations in Table 11, controllability analysis in Table 9, and identical qualitative case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Reporting remains based on the same point estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are retained. For example, Table 3 reports Dream4Drive mAP of 40.7, 43.6, and 44.5 at 1×, 2×, and 3× epochs in both versions; Table 10 retains FVD 31.84 and FID 5.80.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same diffusion definitions, conditioning and fusion formulations, and loss definitions. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about fair training-epoch comparisons, perception improvements from less than 2% synthetic data, and the Dream4Drive and DriveObj3D contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning geometric consistency, shadows and reflections, insertion-location bias, occlusion, and domain gap are unchanged. Appendix E retains the limitation concerning automatically ensuring drivable, collision-free insertion trajectories.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same implementation and training details, including eight H200 GPUs, 2,000 iterations, optimizer settings, loss definitions, and insertion selection. The project address and promised public asset release are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds four works: a multimodal-LLM benchmark survey, Dr.V, PanoSent, and NUS-Emo. The first two replace Wen et al. (2024) in one early-generation citation group; Panacea remains cited and evaluated elsewhere. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Ming Lu's affiliation changes from Xiaomi EV to Peking University and his project-leader marker is removed. Dates and citation labels are updated, while substantive prose and section ordering remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The references now begin on a separate page, leaving whitespace below the conclusion and repaginating the bibliography and appendices. All figures and tables retain their designs, captions, and relative placements.

improvement.justification: In Section 2, v3 replaces a Panacea citation with references whose listed subjects are video-hallucination diagnosis and multimodal-LLM benchmarks, and adds sentiment/emotion-analysis citations to the paired-image-generation claim. Their relevance is unexplained, weakening citation support. Methods, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall decline is limited.
